title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Graph API options for icons, visibility, metadata and labels on custom connectors
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, connector licensing, admin path and schema API are supported. It correctly reports the disagreement between the roadmap status and the May 2026 release note, and distinguishes documented partner-connector visibility controls from unresolved custom-connector details.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans Graph API options to configure icons for custom connectors.
claims.quote: Graph API for custom connectors will provide the options to configure icons, visibility, connection metadata, property descriptions and more semantic labels for improved relevance and UX.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans Graph API options to configure visibility for custom connectors.
claims.quote: Graph API for custom connectors will provide the options to configure icons, visibility, connection metadata, property descriptions and more semantic labels for improved relevance and UX.

claims.quote: Graph API for custom connectors will provide the options to configure icons, visibility, connection metadata, property descriptions and more semantic labels for improved relevance and UX.

claims.where: What's changing; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap describes these options as improving relevance and user experience, rather than introducing new data sources.
claims.quote: Graph API for custom connectors will provide the options to configure icons, visibility, connection metadata, property descriptions and more semantic labels for improved relevance and UX.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: Developers build custom connectors with the Copilot connectors API to index content from their own data sources into Microsoft Graph for Copilot.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors (formerly Microsoft Graph connectors) bring external data into Microsoft Graph and enhance Microsoft 365 intelligent experiences. To build custom connectors, you use the Copilot connectors REST API.

claims.claim: The schema property resource has an optional description property.
claims.quote: description | String | Specifies a human-readable description that explains the purpose, usage, or guidance related to the property. Optional but we recommend that you use this property for queryable properties.

claims.claim: The maximum supported property description length is 200 characters.
claims.quote: The maximum supported length is 200 characters.

claims.claim: Property descriptions help Copilot interpret queries and map them to properties.
claims.quote: This property enhances semantic understanding by helping Copilot interpret queries and accurately map them to properties that results in more relevant and precise responses.

claims.claim: iconUrl is a semantic label that a schema property can carry.
claims.quote: `fileName`, `fileExtension`, `unknownFutureValue`, `containerName`, `containerUrl`, `iconUrl`, `assignedTo`, `dueDate`, `closedDate`, `closedBy`, `reportedBy`

claims.claim: Learn lists title, url and iconUrl as labels to apply for content to surface in Copilot.
claims.quote: The iconUrl, title, and url labels must be applied for content to surface in Copilot.

claims.claim: The release note describing the custom connector Graph API enhancements is dated May 19, 2026.
claims.quote:
May 19, 2026
Updates released between May 5, 2026, May 19, 2026
Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility
Graph API enhancements for custom connector relevance and UX [Web]

claims.claim: The May 19, 2026 release note says developers can now configure the listed custom connector options.
claims.quote: Developers can now configure icons, visibility settings, connection metadata, property descriptions, and semantic labels for custom connectors.

claims.claim: The schema management guide still says support for adding property descriptions to custom connectors is expected in Q4 2025.
claims.quote: Support for adding property descriptions to custom connectors is expected in Q4 2025.

claims.claim: Learn does not identify which API property or setting corresponds to the roadmap's visibility option.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph externalConnection Copilot visibility isEnabled configuration API beta. Read externalConnection v1.0 and beta, beta Update connection, manage-connector and release notes; none explicitly maps the roadmap's visibility option to a property.

claims.claim: Learn does not identify which API property or setting the roadmap specifically means by connection metadata.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors Graph API enhancements icons visibility connection metadata 502537 default admin enable rollout. Read release notes and externalConnection v1.0/beta: metadata properties exist, but no explicit mapping to this roadmap phrase was documented.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors Graph API enhancements icons visibility connection metadata 502537 default admin enable rollout. Read roadmap and May 19 release-note entry: developers can configure options, but neither states an automatic change to existing connectors.

claims.claim: Rich connection descriptions improve the likelihood of content being displayed in Copilot.
claims.quote: Provide meaningful descriptions in the description property when creating connections. Rich descriptions improve the likelihood of content displayed in Copilot.

claims.claim: Semantic labels help Copilot understand schema properties.
claims.quote: These labels help Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Search understand the meaning and role of each property, improving search, summarization, and overall user experience.

claims.claim: Semantic labels help with ranking and relevance.
claims.quote: Semantic labels help with ranking, relevance, and default display templates in search results.

claims.quote: Searched: Graph API enhancements custom connector actions default licensing. Read roadmap, May 19 release-note entry, schema guide and property resource; these describe configuration and relevance, not new autonomous actions.

claims.claim: Creating a schema can take between 5 and 15 minutes.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reindexing items after updating a schema.
claims.quote: After updating your schema, we recommend reindexing items to align them with the latest schema. Without reingestion, item behavior might be inconsistent.

claims.claim: Adding or removing a search capability requires reingestion.

claims.claim: Connection visibility changes can take up to 30 minutes to propagate across Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: After you update the visibility settings at the connection level, allow up to 30 minutes for the changes to propagate across all Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: Assigning a semantic label to a property that does not match its purpose degrades the experience.
claims.quote: Do not assign a label to a property if it doesn't match its purpose—incorrect mappings degrade the experience.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The documented partner-connector Copilot Visibility control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connection > Copilot Visibility.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connection that you want to modify. Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off, and choose Save.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: An API equivalent of the documented partner-connector Copilot Visibility toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph externalConnection Copilot visibility isEnabled configuration API beta; Copilot Visibility Graph API PowerShell. Read manage-connector, externalConnection v1.0/beta and beta Update connection; no operation setting this toggle is documented.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/external/connections/{id}/schema creates or updates the custom connector schema carrying property labels and descriptions.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr/schema
In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a schema object.

claims.claim: An admin UI for setting semantic labels and property descriptions on custom connectors built directly with the Graph API, rather than the connectors SDK, is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: custom connector Graph API not SDK admin center edit semantic labels property descriptions. Read schema guide, manage-connector and custom-connector-sdk-publish; label assignment UI is SDK-specific, and custom schema recommendations do not document editing.

claims.claim: SDK-built custom connectors have an Assign property labels page during admin-center publishing.
claims.quote: When you use the Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors (formerly Microsoft Graph connectors) SDK, you can publish your custom connectors through the Microsoft 365 admin center. On the Assign property labels page, assign semantic labels to your source properties.

claims.claim: Turning off the documented partner-connector Copilot Visibility toggle excludes the connection from Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results.
claims.quote: Admins can control the visibility of partner connectors in Copilot and Copilot Search via a simple toggle. When the visibility is off, the connector is excluded from all Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results and responses.

claims.claim: The documented visibility changes do not affect declarative agents and their data.
claims.quote: The default behavior is visible by default, with changes syncing automatically with search, without affecting declarative agents and their data.

claims.claim: The documented partner-connector visibility control is visible by default.
claims.quote: The default behavior is visible by default, with changes syncing automatically with search, without affecting declarative agents and their data.

claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 admin center provides schema recommendations for published custom connectors. Schema recommendations analyze your connector schema and highlight missing semantic labels for key properties that Copilot relies on to understand, rank, and cite content.
